elements.element: Customer is not subject to any employee non-solicitation restriction.
elements.evidence: The operative clause expressly binds IBM to refrain from soliciting Transferred Employees for twelve months.

elements.element: The employee non-solicitation restriction is mutual, binding both Customer and the counterparty.
elements.evidence: Only IBM is restricted; no reciprocal non-solicitation obligation binds MSL.

elements.element: Covered personnel are limited to personnel directly involved in the services.
elements.evidence: The clause covers all “Transferred Employees” and does not limit coverage to personnel directly involved in the services.

elements.element: The restriction lasts for twelve months from the end of each covered person’s involvement in the services.
elements.evidence: The twelve-month period runs from the Agreement’s Effective Date, not from the end of the relevant person’s involvement.

elements.element: The restriction excludes solicitation or hiring resulting from general advertisements or communications.
elements.evidence: Subsection (b) permits general employment advertising or communications and hiring persons who respond.

elements.element: The restriction excludes unsolicited approaches by personnel.
elements.evidence: Subsection (a) permits employing a person who contacts IBM on their own initiative without solicitation or encouragement by IBM.

elements.element: The clause does not prohibit hiring personnel where no prohibited solicitation occurred.
elements.evidence: The operative prohibition is limited to solicitation, and the carve-outs expressly permit employing or hiring persons who approach independently or respond to general recruiting efforts.

result.reason: The redline only replaces the open-ended term with twelve months from the Effective Date. It still imposes a non-solicit on IBM, defeating the preferred position, and it does not make the restriction mutual, limit personnel to those directly involved in the services, or measure the term from the end of each person’s involvement. Although the existing carve-outs and absence of a no-hire are acceptable, the operative language does not reach either complete position.
